what_happened: The timing-measurement line (20261114-194517-c16g) had a first attempt that finished its producer and checks. It was then held at the verifier because disk was low. A retry (20261116-041223-m3vc) was queued. It re-planned from scratch and failed in planning. That failure tripped the T3 spend pause on the line. At Sri's request ("Resume it"), the the person running Athena lifted the pause by hand. The the person running Athena will stop the drain and resume the kept candidate with athena go, so that only the verifier runs.
cause: Athena treats a stop caused by the environment (low disk at the verifier) as an ordinary failed attempt. It then retries by re-planning from scratch instead of resuming the kept, already-built candidate. The spend guard counts the new planning spend as progress-less spend on the line and pauses it. Nothing tells the guard or the retry path that the first attempt was complete up to the verifier. So the only way forward is for an the person running Athena to lift the pause and run the resume by hand.
other_causes: The retry path has no rule to prefer resuming a kept candidate when the earlier stop was environmental.
The drain was still running while the the person running Athena resumed the job, so the the person running Athena has to stop it first to keep the run verifier-only.
open_hypotheses: The input does not show whether the low-disk attempt's own spend was counted toward the T3 pause, or whether only the failed re-plan was.
The input does not show why retry m3vc re-planned instead of resuming the kept candidate. It could be the default retry mode, or a choice by Athena's failure review or by a person.
contradictions: The event category is overrode-decision, but no decision was matched, and the the person running Athena acted on the owner's explicit request to resume.
The pause was tripped by the retry's planning failure, not directly by the low-disk stop. This fits the class description only partly.
prevention: When a job stops for an environment reason such as low disk and a verified candidate is kept, the next attempt should resume that candidate and run only the missing stage. It should not re-plan. The scope guard should leave spend from environment-stopped attempts out of its progress-less tally, or mark it separately. Athena should also show the retry mode and expected cost before the retry starts. With these in place, the pause would not have tripped and no hand lift would have been needed.
proposed_request: When a job ends or is held for an environment reason (low disk, container restart) and a kept candidate exists with its producer and checks complete, make `athena retry` and the drain's failure review resume that candidate and run only the remaining stages, such as the verifier, instead of re-planning. Show the retry mode (resume or rebuild) and its expected cost before it starts. Make the scope guard exclude spend from attempts that stopped for an environment reason from the progress-less spend that triggers a pause, and record that spend separately. Acceptance: (1) a test with a job held for low disk at the verifier shows that retry resumes the kept candidate and runs only the verifier; (2) a test shows that environment-stopped spend does not trip the T3 pause; (3) the retry output states the mode and expected cost; (4) a CHANGELOG.md entry is added.
